content.text: The licence grant in § 13 meets the preferred position on every material term; the only tension (§ 14.2 Deliverable licence) sits inside the Deliverables-ownership clause and is largely overridden by §§ 13.2–13.3 and 14.3.

input.quote: 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: The grant clause meets the preferred position on all material terms: § 13.1 extends the subscription licence to Customer's Affiliates and to contractors acting on their behalf (and to Authorized Users); § 13.2 makes paid-up software and Vendor Technology (including material embedded in a Deliverable) perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and fully paid for Customer and its Affiliates, with contractor support permitted; and § 13.3 allows transfer to an Affiliate or successor on a permitted assignment and bars Vendor revocation or suspension except for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity. No "revocable at Vendor's discretion" or affiliate/contractor exclusion appears in the grant. Noted but not flagged here: § 14.2 describes the Deliverable licence as "revocable, non-transferable" and limited to the Order Form term. That language is substantially constrained by § 13.3 (no revocation absent uncured material breach; transfer to Affiliate/successor permitted), § 14.3 (embedded Vendor Technology carries the § 13.2 perpetual licence) and § 10.1 (rights in accepted Deliverables survive). The residual issue is Vendor's ownership of Customer-specific Deliverables, which belongs to the IP-ownership rule rather than being duplicated under the licence-scope rule.
